roadmaps.title: Front-End Developer
roadmaps.goal: Build and ship interfaces people actually use
roadmaps.blurb: From a blank HTML file to a component-driven app you can deploy.

units.title: The page itself
units.note: What the browser is given.

units.title: The language
units.note: Making it move.

units.title: Working at scale
units.note: What teams reach for once pages get big.

units.title: Getting it out
units.note: The half of the job nobody teaches.

path.title: HTML
path.why: Structure first. Everything else — styling, scripting, screen readers — attaches to it.

path.title: CSS
path.why: The rules that turn structure into something worth looking at.

path.title: The box model
path.why: Why your element is 8px wider than you asked for. Learn it once, stop guessing.

path.title: Flexbox & Grid
path.why: How real layouts are composed. Almost every alignment bug is a gap here.

path.title: Responsive design
path.why: One layout, every screen. Not a phase of the work — a property of it.

path.title: JavaScript
path.why: The only language the browser runs. Everything else compiles down to it.

path.title: The DOM
path.why: The page as an object you can read and change. This is what a framework is hiding.

path.title: Events
path.why: How a click becomes code. Bubbling explains most 'why did that fire' mysteries.

path.title: Modern JS
path.why: Destructuring, modules, arrow functions — the syntax every tutorial assumes.

path.title: Async & promises
path.why: Nothing waits in a browser. Understanding why is the difference between working and lucky.

path.title: Fetch & APIs
path.why: Real apps show real data. This is where the network enters your mental model.

path.title: npm & modules
path.why: How code you didn't write gets into code you did.

path.title: Git
path.why: Undo for your whole project, and the only way more than one person can work.

path.title: React
path.why: UI as functions of data. The mental shift is the point, not the syntax.

path.title: State
path.why: Where truth lives and who's allowed to change it. Most UI bugs are really this.

path.title: Effects & data fetching
path.why: Talking to the outside world without tearing the UI. Easy to get subtly wrong.

path.title: Routing
path.why: Turning one page into an app with a back button that works.

path.title: Accessibility
path.why: Keyboard, contrast, labels. Building for everyone rather than for people like you.

path.title: Performance
path.why: Users leave slow pages. Learn to measure before you optimise.

path.title: Build & deploy
path.why: Work nobody can visit isn't finished.

branches.title: TypeScript
branches.why: Types catch the mistakes your users would have found for you.

branches.title: Tailwind CSS
branches.why: Styling without leaving the markup, once you already know CSS.

branches.title: Component testing
branches.why: Confidence that a change didn't quietly break something else.

branches.title: Server rendering
branches.why: Faster first paint and pages search engines can read.

branches.title: Animation
branches.why: Motion that explains what changed instead of decorating it.

roadmaps.title: Back-End Developer
roadmaps.goal: Build services that hold data and stay up
roadmaps.blurb: Requests, storage, and the failure modes nobody warns you about.

units.title: Groundwork
units.note: A language and how the internet actually moves.

units.title: Data
units.note: Where state lives.

units.title: Interfaces
units.note: How the outside world asks for things.

units.title: Production
units.note: What changes when real people depend on it.

path.title: A server language
path.why: Pick one — Node, Python, Go — and get fluent. The concepts transfer; the syntax doesn't matter yet.

path.title: The terminal
path.why: Servers have no windows. This is the interface.

path.title: Git
path.why: Branching, merging, reading history to find when something broke.

path.title: HTTP
path.why: Methods, status codes, headers. Most 'weird bug' reports are HTTP misunderstandings.

path.title: SQL
path.why: The language of data that has to be right. Still the highest-leverage thing to learn here.

path.title: Data modelling
path.why: Schema decisions outlive your code. Getting them wrong is the expensive kind of wrong.

path.title: Indexes & queries
path.why: Why the same query is instant on your laptop and dead in production.

path.title: Transactions
path.why: How two things happen together or not at all. The idea behind every money bug.

path.title: REST APIs
path.why: The default shape of a service, and the conventions that make it predictable.

path.title: Validation
path.why: Never trust input. Every boundary is a place to be strict.

path.title: Auth
path.why: Sessions, tokens, hashing. The area where a small mistake is a large incident.

path.title: Caching
path.why: The cheapest speed there is, and a fine way to serve stale data forever.

path.title: Queues & jobs
path.why: Work that shouldn't happen inside a request. Email, exports, anything slow.

path.title: Logging & metrics
path.why: You cannot fix what you cannot see. Do this before you need it.

path.title: Testing
path.why: The thing that lets you change code you no longer remember writing.

path.title: Deployment
path.why: From your machine to a machine strangers can reach.

branches.title: NoSQL
branches.why: When the shape of your data genuinely isn't tabular.

branches.title: GraphQL
branches.why: Letting clients ask for exactly what they need — and the costs of that.

branches.title: WebSockets
branches.why: When the server needs to speak first.

branches.title: Rate limiting
branches.why: Staying up when someone points a script at you.

roadmaps.title: Python
roadmaps.goal: Write Python you'd be happy to hand someone else
roadmaps.blurb: The language, then the parts that separate scripts from software.

units.title: The language
units.note: Enough to be dangerous.

units.title: Structure
units.note: Enough to be trusted.

units.title: Real programs
units.note: Enough to ship.

path.title: Syntax & types
path.why: Numbers, strings, truthiness. Python's rules are few and worth knowing exactly.

path.title: Lists, dicts, sets
path.why: Choosing the right one is most of what makes Python fast or slow.

path.title: Control flow
path.why: Loops and comprehensions. The comprehension is the idiom you'll read everywhere.

path.title: Functions
path.why: Arguments, defaults, scope. The mutable-default trap catches everyone once.

path.title: Modules & imports
path.why: How a file becomes a library, and why circular imports hurt.

path.title: Classes
path.why: When state and behaviour belong together — and when a function was enough.

path.title: Exceptions
path.why: Failing loudly and on purpose beats returning None and hoping.

path.title: Type hints
path.why: Documentation the tools can check. Worth it the moment someone else reads the code.

path.title: Environments & packaging
path.why: Dependencies that don't leak between projects. Do this early; it saves days.

path.title: Testing
path.why: The safety net that makes refactoring possible instead of frightening.

path.title: Files & data formats
path.why: CSV, JSON, paths. Most real programs are shaped by their input.

path.title: Async
path.why: Waiting on many things at once, and why threads aren't usually the answer here.

branches.title: The standard library
branches.why: The batteries. Reading it is the fastest way to get better.

branches.title: Command-line tools
branches.why: Turning a script into something with a real interface.

branches.title: Profiling
branches.why: Measuring before optimising, because your guess is usually wrong.

roadmaps.title: SQL & Databases
roadmaps.goal: Ask hard questions of real data
roadmaps.blurb: From SELECT to query plans — the skill with the longest shelf life in software.

units.title: Asking
units.note: Getting data out.

units.title: Shaping
units.note: Combining and summarising.

units.title: Designing
units.note: Deciding how it's stored.

path.title: SELECT & WHERE
path.why: Where every query starts. Filtering well is most of the job.

path.title: Sorting & limiting
path.why: Ordering, paging, and why OFFSET gets slow on big tables.

path.title: NULL
path.why: Not zero, not empty, and not equal to itself. The source of countless quiet bugs.

path.title: Joins
path.why: Inner, left, and the accidental cross join that returns a million rows.

path.title: GROUP BY
path.why: Turning rows into answers. Where analysis actually happens.

path.title: Subqueries & CTEs
path.why: Naming intermediate steps so a hard query stays readable.

path.title: Window functions
path.why: Running totals and rankings without losing the individual rows.

path.title: Schema design
path.why: Tables, keys, relationships. The decisions your code will live inside.

path.title: Normalisation
path.why: Storing each fact once — and knowing when to break the rule deliberately.

path.title: Constraints
path.why: Letting the database refuse impossible data instead of trusting every writer.

path.title: Indexes
path.why: Why a query is instant or unbearable, and the write cost of every index.

path.title: Query plans
path.why: Reading what the database decided to do. The end of guessing.

branches.title: Transactions & isolation
branches.why: Concurrent writes, and the anomalies each isolation level still allows.

branches.title: Migrations
branches.why: Changing a schema that's in use, without downtime or data loss.

branches.title: JSON in SQL
branches.why: Semi-structured columns, and when they're a shortcut you'll pay for.

roadmaps.title: Machine Learning
roadmaps.goal: Understand how models learn, not just how to call them
roadmaps.blurb: The maths, the code, and the models — in the order they build on each other.

units.title: The maths
units.note: Skippable right up until it isn't.

units.title: The tools
units.note: Where the data lives.

units.title: The models
units.note: Simple ones first, and they're often enough.

units.title: Deep learning
units.note: What the last decade was about.

path.title: Algebra
path.why: The grammar of every equation ahead.

path.title: Linear algebra
path.why: Vectors and matrices are how data and weights are stored. Not optional.

path.title: Calculus
path.why: A derivative is how a model knows which way to improve.

path.title: Probability & statistics
path.why: Reasoning under uncertainty — which is the whole job.

path.title: Python
path.why: The language the field runs on.

path.title: NumPy & pandas
path.why: Loading, cleaning and computing on real data. Most of your time goes here.

path.title: Visualisation
path.why: Looking at the data before modelling it catches errors nothing else will.

path.title: What learning means
path.why: Features, labels, generalisation. The framing everything else hangs on.

path.title: Train/test splits
path.why: How you avoid fooling yourself. The single most common beginner mistake.

path.title: Linear regression
path.why: The simplest real model, and the one every other one is compared against.

path.title: Gradient descent
path.why: The optimiser under almost everything. Worth deriving once by hand.

path.title: Classification
path.why: Predicting categories, and why accuracy is a misleading score.

path.title: Overfitting
path.why: Why your model was brilliant in testing and useless in production.

path.title: Trees & ensembles
path.why: What actually wins on tabular data. Often beats a neural network here.

path.title: Neural networks
path.why: Layers of simple functions composing into complicated ones.

path.title: Backpropagation
path.why: The chain rule, applied at scale. Understand it once and the rest demystifies.

path.title: Convolutional nets
path.why: Exploiting the fact that nearby pixels are related.

path.title: Attention
path.why: Letting a model decide what to look at. The idea behind the last decade.

path.title: Transformers
path.why: The architecture behind modern language models, and why it scaled.

branches.title: Feature engineering
branches.why: Often worth more than a better model. Underrated and unglamorous.

branches.title: Clustering
branches.why: Finding structure when nothing is labelled.

branches.title: Large language models
branches.why: Prompting, fine-tuning, and what they genuinely cannot do.

branches.title: Putting models in production
branches.why: The part where a notebook has to become a service that stays up.

branches.title: Bias & fairness
branches.why: A model trained on the past will reproduce it. That's a design problem, not a footnote.

roadmaps.title: DevOps & Infrastructure
roadmaps.goal: Run software reliably, and know when it isn't
roadmaps.blurb: The path from 'works on my machine' to 'works at 3am unattended'.

units.title: The machine
units.note: What you're actually deploying onto.

units.title: Packaging
units.note: Making software portable.

units.title: Automation
units.note: Doing it the same way every time.

units.title: Knowing
units.note: Reliability is mostly information.

path.title: Linux
path.why: Almost everything runs on it. Processes, permissions, the filesystem.

path.title: Shell scripting
path.why: Automating the ten commands you keep typing.

path.title: Networking
path.why: DNS, ports, TLS. 'It can't connect' is almost always one of these three.

path.title: Containers
path.why: Shipping the environment with the code. The idea that ended most deploy arguments.

path.title: Multi-container apps
path.why: An app is rarely one process. Running the whole thing locally.

path.title: Registries & images
path.why: Where builds live, and why image size is a real cost.

path.title: CI
path.why: Tests that run whether or not anyone remembers to run them.

path.title: CD
path.why: Deploying often, in small pieces, so each one is boring.

path.title: Infrastructure as code
path.why: Servers you can recreate from a file instead of from memory.

path.title: Orchestration
path.why: Many containers, many machines, one description of what should be running.

path.title: Monitoring
path.why: Metrics and dashboards: the difference between knowing and hoping.

path.title: Alerting
path.why: Waking the right person for the right reason, and nobody otherwise.

path.title: Backups & recovery
path.why: A backup you have never restored is a rumour.

path.title: Secrets
path.why: Credentials out of the repo, out of the logs, and rotatable.

branches.title: Kubernetes
branches.why: The industry default for orchestration — and a lot of complexity to earn.

branches.title: Distributed tracing
branches.why: Following one request across many services.

branches.title: Failure testing
branches.why: Breaking it on purpose, on a Tuesday, instead of by accident on a Sunday.

roadmaps.title: System Design
roadmaps.goal: Reason about systems too big to hold in your head
roadmaps.blurb: The trade-offs behind every architecture diagram, in the order they start to matter.

units.title: Primitives
units.note: The parts everything is assembled from.

units.title: Scaling
units.note: What breaks first, and what you do about it.

units.title: The hard parts
units.note: Where distributed systems stop being intuitive.

path.title: Latency numbers
path.why: Memory, disk, network, across an ocean. Knowing the orders of magnitude settles most arguments.

path.title: Storage engines
path.why: How a database actually writes to disk, and why that shapes what it's good at.

path.title: Caching strategies
path.why: Read-through, write-through, invalidation. Cheap wins with expensive failure modes.

path.title: Load balancing
path.why: Spreading work, and what happens to the requests in flight when a box dies.

path.title: Replication
path.why: More copies means more reads and more ways to disagree.

path.title: Sharding
path.why: Splitting data that no longer fits, and picking a key you won't regret.

path.title: Async & queues
path.why: Decoupling producers from consumers so a spike becomes a backlog, not an outage.

path.title: Consistency models
path.why: Strong, eventual, causal. Most 'it showed the old value' bugs are a choice made here.

path.title: Idempotency & retries
path.why: Networks deliver twice. Designing for that is cheaper than detecting it.

path.title: Backpressure
path.why: Refusing work you can't do beats collapsing while accepting all of it.

path.title: Failure & degradation
path.why: Deciding in advance which features die first, while you're calm.

branches.title: Consensus
branches.why: How several machines agree on one answer. The foundation under leader election.

branches.title: Event sourcing
branches.why: Storing what happened rather than what is. Powerful, and hard to walk back.

branches.title: Multi-region
branches.why: Serving users a continent away, and the consistency bill that comes with it.

roadmaps.title: NEET UG
roadmaps.goal: Cover the syllabus in an order that actually builds
roadmaps.blurb: Physics, Chemistry and Biology as one dependency graph — not three lists of chapters.

units.title: Biology — Class 11
units.note: Half the paper starts here. Structure before function.

units.title: Biology — Class 12
units.note: Genetics, ecology and the highest-yield chapters in the exam.

units.title: Chemistry — Class 11
units.note: Physical and organic foundations everything later leans on.

units.title: Chemistry — Class 12
units.note: Where organic mechanisms and coordination chemistry pay off.

units.title: Physics — Class 11
units.note: Mechanics. The subject most students underestimate.

units.title: Physics — Class 12
units.note: Electricity, magnetism and optics — reliably heavy in the paper.

path.title: The Living World
path.why: Taxonomy and nomenclature. Short, scoring, and often skipped for being dull.

path.title: Biological Classification
path.why: Five kingdoms, viruses, lichens. Dense with directly-askable facts.

path.title: Plant Kingdom
path.why: Algae to angiosperms. Life cycles here recur throughout Botany.

path.title: Animal Kingdom
path.why: Phylum characteristics and examples. Consistently one of the highest-yield chapters.

path.title: Morphology of Flowering Plants
path.why: The vocabulary the rest of Botany is written in. Learn the terms properly once.

path.title: Anatomy of Flowering Plants
path.why: Tissues and their arrangement. Diagram-heavy, and diagrams are what get asked.

path.title: Structural Organisation in Animals
path.why: Tissue types, and the earthworm-cockroach-frog comparisons.

path.title: Cell: The Unit of Life
path.why: Every later chapter assumes it. Organelles, membranes, prokaryote versus eukaryote.

path.title: Biomolecules
path.why: Proteins, enzymes, nucleic acids. Bridges directly into Chemistry and into Genetics.

path.title: Cell Cycle & Cell Division
path.why: Mitosis and meiosis. Genetics is unlearnable without meiosis being solid.

path.title: Photosynthesis
path.why: The light and dark reactions, C3 versus C4. Reliably examined every year.

path.title: Respiration in Plants
path.why: Glycolysis, Krebs, ETC. Learn the ATP arithmetic; it gets asked numerically.

path.title: Plant Growth & Development
path.why: Hormones and their effects. Small chapter, easy marks.

path.title: Digestion & Absorption
path.why: Human physiology begins. Enzymes, disorders, and the deficiency questions.

path.title: Breathing & Exchange of Gases
path.why: Transport of gases and the dissociation curve — a favourite for graph questions.

path.title: Body Fluids & Circulation
path.why: The cardiac cycle and ECG. Dense, diagram-driven, and heavily weighted.

path.title: Excretory Products
path.why: The nephron in detail. Counter-current mechanism is the part that gets asked.

path.title: Locomotion & Movement
path.why: Muscle contraction at molecular level, plus joints and skeletal disorders.

path.title: Neural Control & Coordination
path.why: Action potential and synapse. Overlaps usefully with Physics electricity.

path.title: Chemical Coordination
path.why: Endocrine glands and hormones. Pure recall — build a table and drill it.

path.title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
path.why: Embryo sac, double fertilisation, apomixis. Very high yield, entirely learnable.

path.title: Human Reproduction
path.why: Gametogenesis and the menstrual cycle. Diagrams and sequences dominate.

path.title: Reproductive Health
path.why: Contraception and ART. Short, factual, frequently asked.

path.title: Principles of Inheritance
path.why: Mendel, linkage, pedigrees. Problem-solving, not recall — practise, don't read.

path.title: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
path.why: Replication, transcription, translation, lac operon. Arguably the single heaviest chapter.

path.title: Evolution
path.why: Hardy-Weinberg gets asked numerically. The rest is a timeline worth memorising.

path.title: Human Health & Disease
path.why: Immunity, pathogens, and the disease-organism pairs. Straight recall, lots of it.

path.title: Microbes in Human Welfare
path.why: Named organisms and their products. Make the table; the questions come from it.

path.title: Biotechnology: Principles
path.why: Restriction enzymes, vectors, PCR. Follows straight from molecular biology.

path.title: Biotechnology: Applications
path.why: Bt crops, RNAi, insulin, gene therapy. Case-by-case; each one is a question.

path.title: Organisms & Populations
path.why: Population interactions and growth curves. The equations do get asked.

path.title: Ecosystem
path.why: Energy flow, pyramids, productivity. Numerical and very scoring.

path.title: Biodiversity & Conservation
path.why: Patterns, hotspots, and named conservation efforts. Cheap marks late in prep.

path.title: Some Basic Concepts
path.why: Mole concept and stoichiometry. Get this wrong and every calculation after it is wrong.

path.title: Structure of Atom
path.why: Quantum numbers and configurations — the basis of the whole periodic table.

path.title: Classification & Periodicity
path.why: Trends you can reason from instead of memorising. Pays back all year.

path.title: Chemical Bonding
path.why: Hybridisation, VSEPR, MOT. Feeds Inorganic and Organic in equal measure.

path.title: Thermodynamics
path.why: Enthalpy, entropy, spontaneity. Overlaps with Physics; sign conventions differ — watch that.

path.title: Equilibrium
path.why: Kc/Kp, acids and bases, pH, buffers. Two chapters' worth of marks in one.

path.title: Redox Reactions
path.why: Oxidation numbers and balancing. Prerequisite for Electrochemistry.

path.title: s-Block Elements
path.why: Alkali and alkaline earth metals. Reasoning from periodicity beats rote here.

path.title: p-Block (Groups 13–14)
path.why: Boron and carbon families. Anomalous behaviour is the examinable part.

path.title: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles
path.why: Inductive and resonance effects, intermediates, nomenclature. Organic is unlearnable without it.

path.title: Hydrocarbons
path.why: Alkanes to aromatics, and the first real mechanisms. Where organic starts to click.

path.title: Solutions
path.why: Colligative properties. Formula-driven and reliably scoring.

path.title: Electrochemistry
path.why: Nernst, conductance, electrolysis. Sits on redox and thermodynamics together.

path.title: Chemical Kinetics
path.why: Rate laws, order, Arrhenius. Graph-reading questions are common.

path.title: p-Block (Groups 15–18)
path.why: Nitrogen through the noble gases. Heavy on named compounds and preparations.

path.title: d- and f-Block Elements
path.why: Transition metals, colour, magnetism, and lanthanide contraction.

path.title: Coordination Compounds
path.why: Isomerism, CFT, nomenclature. Consistently one of the best-value chapters.

path.title: Haloalkanes & Haloarenes
path.why: SN1 versus SN2 — the first mechanism you must reason about, not recall.

path.title: Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers
path.why: Conversions and named reactions. Central to the organic conversion questions.

path.title: Aldehydes, Ketones & Acids
path.why: The busiest chapter in organic. Aldol, Cannizzaro, and a dozen named reactions.

path.title: Amines
path.why: Basicity and diazonium chemistry — the route to most aromatic conversions.

path.title: Biomolecules
path.why: Carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins. Overlaps with Biology — study them together.

path.title: Units & Measurement
path.why: Dimensional analysis and error. Cheap marks, and it catches wrong answers later.

path.title: Kinematics
path.why: Motion in a line and a plane. Graphs and vectors — the language of everything ahead.

path.title: Laws of Motion
path.why: Free-body diagrams and friction. If mechanics is shaky, it starts here.

path.title: Work, Energy & Power
path.why: Conservation arguments that solve problems force analysis can't.

path.title: Rotational Motion
path.why: Moment of inertia and torque. Hard, heavily weighted, and worth the time.

path.title: Gravitation
path.why: Orbits and potential energy. Follows directly from circular motion.

path.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids
path.why: Stress, strain, moduli. Short and formula-driven.

path.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
path.why: Bernoulli, viscosity, surface tension. Applications get asked more than derivations.

path.title: Thermal Properties of Matter
path.why: Expansion, calorimetry, conduction. Straightforward marks.

path.title: Thermodynamics
path.why: Laws, processes, engines. Compare carefully with the Chemistry treatment.

path.title: Kinetic Theory
path.why: Gas equations and degrees of freedom. Small chapter, quick returns.

path.title: Oscillations
path.why: SHM. Its mathematics reappears in AC circuits and in waves.

path.title: Waves
path.why: Superposition, beats, Doppler. Sets up wave optics later.

path.title: Electric Charges & Fields
path.why: Coulomb and Gauss. Symmetry arguments do most of the work.

path.title: Potential & Capacitance
path.why: Potential, then capacitors in combination. Very reliably examined.

path.title: Current Electricity
path.why: Kirchhoff, meter bridge, potentiometer. Among the highest-yield chapters in the paper.

path.title: Moving Charges & Magnetism
path.why: Biot-Savart, Ampère, the cyclotron. Geometry-heavy — draw everything.

path.title: Magnetism & Matter
path.why: Materials and Earth's field. Mostly recall.

path.title: Electromagnetic Induction
path.why: Faraday and Lenz. Sign conventions are where marks are lost.

path.title: Alternating Current
path.why: LCR, resonance, phasors. Reuses the SHM mathematics directly.

path.title: Electromagnetic Waves
path.why: The spectrum and its uses. Short, factual, easy.

path.title: Ray Optics
path.why: Mirrors, lenses, instruments. Sign convention errors cost more marks here than anywhere.

path.title: Wave Optics
path.why: Interference, diffraction, polarisation. Rests on Waves.

path.title: Dual Nature of Radiation
path.why: Photoelectric effect and de Broglie. Small, formula-driven, dependable.

path.title: Atoms
path.why: Bohr model and spectra. Pairs directly with Chemistry's Structure of Atom.

path.title: Nuclei
path.why: Binding energy, decay, mass defect. Numerical and consistently asked.

path.title: Semiconductors
path.why: Diodes, rectifiers, logic gates. Self-contained and quick to secure.

branches.title: Previous years' papers
branches.why: The single highest-return activity in the whole preparation. Start earlier than feels comfortable.

branches.title: NCERT line-by-line (Biology)
branches.why: NEET Biology is drawn from NCERT wording. Reading it as the source, not a summary, is the strategy.

branches.title: Diagram practice
branches.why: Labelled diagrams appear directly as questions. Drawing beats re-reading.

branches.title: Full-length mocks
branches.why: 180 questions in 180 minutes is a stamina skill, trained separately from knowing content.

branches.title: An error notebook
branches.why: Re-reading what you know is comfortable; revisiting what you got wrong is what moves the score.

roadmaps.title: JEE Main & Advanced
roadmaps.goal: Build the Maths that makes the Physics possible
roadmaps.blurb: Three subjects, one dependency graph — including the cross-subject links that decide who struggles.

units.title: Mathematics — Class 11
units.note: Algebra and trigonometry. The toolkit.

units.title: Mathematics — Class 12
units.note: Calculus. Roughly half of Maths, and the half Physics needs.

units.title: Physics — Class 11
units.note: Mechanics, and it is where the exam is won or lost.

units.title: Physics — Class 12
units.note: Electromagnetism and modern physics.

units.title: Chemistry — Class 11
units.note: Physical and organic foundations.

units.title: Chemistry — Class 12
units.note: Where the marks are most predictable.

path.title: Sets, Relations & Functions
path.why: Domain and range discipline. Half of all calculus errors are really function-domain errors.

path.title: Trigonometric Functions
path.why: Identities and equations. Physics uses these constantly and without warning.

path.title: Quadratics & Complex Numbers
path.why: Roots, Argand plane, rotation. Complex numbers reappear in AC circuits.

path.title: Permutations & Combinations
path.why: Counting properly. Short chapter, and a hard one to bluff.

path.title: Binomial Theorem
path.why: General term and expansions. Feeds series and approximations.

path.title: Sequences & Series
path.why: AP, GP, and summation technique. Turns up inside other chapters more than alone.

path.title: Straight Lines
path.why: Coordinate geometry's grammar. Everything conic sits on it.

path.title: Conic Sections
path.why: Circle, parabola, ellipse, hyperbola. Heavily weighted and very pattern-based.

path.title: Vectors
path.why: Dot and cross products. Physics is written in this language from mechanics onward.

path.title: Limits & Derivatives
path.why: The gateway to calculus. Rushing this makes all of Class 12 harder than it needs to be.

path.title: Probability
path.why: Conditional probability and Bayes. Small, self-contained, reliably examined.

path.title: Matrices & Determinants
path.why: Operations, inverses, systems of equations. Mechanical marks once drilled.

path.title: Inverse Trigonometry
path.why: Principal values and the domain traps that make answers wrong by a sign.

path.title: Continuity & Differentiability
path.why: Where derivatives exist and why. Advanced loves the edge cases.

path.title: Applications of Derivatives
path.why: Maxima, minima, tangents, rates. The most directly applicable chapter in Maths.

path.title: Integrals
path.why: Techniques and definite integrals. The largest single block of marks in Maths.

path.title: Applications of Integrals
path.why: Area under curves. Straightforward once integration is fluent.

path.title: Differential Equations
path.why: Separable and linear forms. Physics uses these for decay and circuits.

path.title: 3D Geometry
path.why: Lines and planes in space. Almost purely formulaic — high return per hour.

path.title: Units, Dimensions & Errors
path.why: Dimensional checking catches wrong answers for free, all exam long.

path.title: Kinematics
path.why: Relative motion and projectiles — done properly with vectors, not memorised formulae.

path.title: Laws of Motion
path.why: Free-body diagrams, constraints, pseudo-forces. The foundation of the whole paper.

path.title: Work, Energy & Power
path.why: Conservation, and variable forces — which is where the calculus enters.

path.title: Centre of Mass & Collisions
path.why: Momentum conservation. Advanced combines it with rotation constantly.

path.title: Rotational Dynamics
path.why: The hardest chapter in Class 11 Physics and among the most heavily weighted. Needs integration.

path.title: Gravitation
path.why: Fields, potential, orbits. Good practice for electrostatics' identical mathematics.

path.title: Simple Harmonic Motion
path.why: Learn it as a differential equation, not a set of formulae — it returns in AC and waves.

path.title: Elasticity
path.why: Stress, strain, moduli. Short and mechanical.

path.title: Fluid Mechanics
path.why: Bernoulli, viscosity, surface tension. Conceptual questions outnumber numerical ones.

path.title: Heat & Thermodynamics
path.why: Processes, engines, entropy. Compare with the Chemistry version — conventions differ.

path.title: Kinetic Theory
path.why: Degrees of freedom and mean free path. Small and dependable.

path.title: Waves & Sound
path.why: Standing waves, beats, Doppler. Organ pipes and strings recur every year.

path.title: Electrostatics
path.why: Gauss's law with symmetry. Mathematically identical to gravitation — reuse that.

path.title: Capacitance
path.why: Combinations, dielectrics, energy. Circuit-reduction skill more than physics.

path.title: Current Electricity
path.why: Kirchhoff and instruments. High weight in Main and endlessly combinable in Advanced.

path.title: Magnetic Effects of Current
path.why: Biot-Savart and Ampère. Cross products from Maths, used in anger.

path.title: Electromagnetic Induction
path.why: Faraday, Lenz, self and mutual inductance. Sign discipline is everything.

path.title: Alternating Current
path.why: Phasors and resonance — SHM and complex numbers in new clothes.

path.title: Electromagnetic Waves
path.why: Spectrum and displacement current. Short, factual, quick marks.

path.title: Ray Optics
path.why: Lenses, mirrors, prisms, instruments. Formula-heavy and very scoring.

path.title: Wave Optics
path.why: YDSE, thin films, diffraction. Rests on Waves being solid.

path.title: Modern Physics
path.why: Photoelectric effect, Bohr, nuclei. Highest marks-per-hour in the paper.

path.title: Semiconductors
path.why: Diodes, transistors, gates. Self-contained; secure it early and revisit rarely.

path.title: Mole Concept & Stoichiometry
path.why: Every numerical in Physical Chemistry depends on it. No exceptions.

path.title: Atomic Structure
path.why: Quantum numbers and orbitals. Explains periodicity rather than listing it.

path.title: Periodic Properties
path.why: Trends you can derive. Saves memorising Inorganic later.

path.title: Chemical Bonding
path.why: Hybridisation, VSEPR, MOT. Feeds Organic and Inorganic in equal measure.

path.title: Gaseous State
path.why: Ideal and real gases, van der Waals. Short and formulaic.

path.title: Thermodynamics & Thermochemistry
path.why: Enthalpy, entropy, Gibbs. Sign conventions differ from Physics — note it once.

path.title: Equilibrium & Ionic Equilibrium
path.why: Kc/Kp, pH, buffers, solubility. Two chapters of marks; consistently examined.

path.title: Redox Reactions
path.why: Oxidation states and balancing. Prerequisite for Electrochemistry.

path.title: Organic: General Principles
path.why: Electronic effects, intermediates, stability. Organic is memorisation without it and logic with it.

path.title: Isomerism & Stereochemistry
path.why: R/S, E/Z, chirality. Advanced asks this directly and often.

path.title: Hydrocarbons
path.why: The first real mechanisms — addition, substitution, aromatic behaviour.

path.title: s-Block & Hydrogen
path.why: Reason from periodicity rather than memorising reaction lists.

path.title: p-Block (13–14)
path.why: Boron and carbon families, and their anomalies.

path.title: Solid State
path.why: Unit cells and packing efficiency. Almost purely numerical — very scoring.

path.title: Solutions
path.why: Colligative properties and Raoult's law. Formula-driven marks.

path.title: Electrochemistry
path.why: Nernst, conductance, electrolysis. Redox and thermodynamics together.

path.title: Chemical Kinetics
path.why: Order, rate laws, Arrhenius. Graph interpretation is the examined skill.

path.title: Surface Chemistry
path.why: Adsorption, colloids, catalysis. Mostly recall, quick to secure.

path.title: p-Block (15–18)
path.why: Nitrogen to noble gases. Preparations and structures dominate.

path.title: d- & f-Block
path.why: Transition metals, colour, magnetic behaviour, lanthanide contraction.

path.title: Coordination Compounds
path.why: Isomerism, CFT, magnetic moments. One of the best-value chapters in the paper.

path.title: Haloalkanes & Haloarenes
path.why: SN1 versus SN2 with stereochemistry. Reasoning, not recall.

path.title: Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers
path.why: Central to the conversion questions that appear every year.

path.title: Carbonyl Compounds
path.why: Aldehydes, ketones, acids and a dozen named reactions. The busiest organic chapter.

path.title: Amines
path.why: Basicity order and diazonium salts — the route to most aromatic conversions.

path.title: Biomolecules & Polymers
path.why: Largely factual. Low weight, but cheap marks near the exam.

path.title: Qualitative Analysis
path.why: Salt analysis and functional group tests. Asked directly, and easy to neglect.

branches.title: Previous years' papers
branches.why: The highest-return activity available. Papers teach the examiner's habits, which no textbook does.

branches.title: Multi-chapter problems
branches.why: What separates Advanced from Main: one problem needing rotation and energy and calculus at once.

branches.title: Timed sectional tests
branches.why: Main is as much a speed exam as a knowledge one. Accuracy under a clock is a separate skill.

branches.title: An error notebook
branches.why: The one habit that most reliably raises a plateaued score. Revisit mistakes, not comfort topics.

branches.title: A formula sheet you wrote
branches.why: Writing it is the revision. A downloaded one is somebody else's memory.

roadmaps.title: Play the Guitar
roadmaps.goal: Play songs people recognise, and know why they work
roadmaps.blurb: Proof the map works for anything — not just code and exams.

units.title: The hands
units.note: Physical before theoretical.

units.title: Songs
units.note: The reason you picked it up.

units.title: Why it works
units.note: Where playing becomes understanding.

path.title: Tuning
path.why: An out-of-tune guitar teaches your ear the wrong thing.

path.title: Open chords
path.why: Five or six shapes cover a startling number of songs.

path.title: Chord changes
path.why: The actual skill. Clean changes matter more than knowing more chords.

path.title: Strumming patterns
path.why: Rhythm is what makes it sound like the record.

path.title: Your first song
path.why: Finishing one whole song teaches more than practising ten fragments.

path.title: Barre chords
path.why: The same shapes anywhere on the neck. Unlocks most of the rest.

path.title: Keys
path.why: Why certain chords sound like they belong together.

path.title: Progressions
path.why: The handful of sequences behind a surprising share of popular music.

path.title: Scales
path.why: Where melody comes from, and how to improvise without guessing.

path.title: Playing by ear
path.why: Working a song out yourself. The point at which you stop needing tabs.

branches.title: Fingerpicking
branches.why: Melody and accompaniment at once.

branches.title: Using a capo
branches.why: Any song in any key without learning new shapes.

branches.title: Recording yourself
branches.why: The fastest, least comfortable way to improve.

guides.title: How to actually prepare for NEET
guides.subtitle: What the paper rewards, in what order to build it, and which advice to ignore.
guides.caveat: NTA has revised the NEET syllabus more than once in recent years, removing whole chapters. This roadmap covers the stable core — but check the official syllabus for your exam year before you decide to skip anything, and before you decide to study anything that isn't in it.

sections.title: The shape of the paper
sections.body:
Biology is half the exam. That single fact should drive your timetable, and for most students it doesn't.

- **Biology** — roughly half the marks, split Botany and Zoology
- **Chemistry** — roughly a quarter
- **Physics** — roughly a quarter

There is negative marking, so an unsure guess has a real cost. Attempting fewer questions with higher accuracy routinely beats attempting everything, and almost nobody believes this until they've seen their own mock analysis.

The consequence: Biology is where the marks are, Physics is where students lose them, and Chemistry is the most predictable of the three. Plan accordingly rather than dividing your day into three equal parts.

sections.title: Biology: NCERT is the syllabus, not a summary of it
sections.body:
NEET Biology questions are drawn from NCERT, frequently from its exact wording — including sentences in boxes, captions under diagrams, and lines most students skim.

Read NCERT as the primary source. A coaching module is a useful supplement and a poor substitute; if the two disagree, NCERT is what the paper follows.

Concretely:
- Read line by line, including diagram labels and example boxes
- Convert every list into a table you wrote yourself — plant families, hormones, diseases and their pathogens, microbes and their products
- Draw the diagrams. Labelled diagrams appear directly as questions, and drawing one is worth three readings of it

**Genetics and Molecular Basis of Inheritance** carry the most weight and are the least like the rest of Biology: they're problem-solving, not recall. Practise them the way you'd practise Physics.

sections.title: Physics: the subject that decides your rank
sections.body:
Most students who miss their target miss it in Physics, and the reason is almost always the same — they moved on from Mechanics before it was solid.

Class 11 Mechanics is not a chapter you clear and leave behind. Laws of Motion, Work-Energy and Rotational Motion underpin everything after them, and a shaky free-body diagram in September is a wrong answer in May.

What works:
- Solve without looking at solutions for longer than is comfortable. Reading a solution feels like learning and mostly isn't
- Keep the sign conventions for Ray Optics and for Induction written down somewhere you'll see them. More marks are lost to signs than to concepts
- Do the numerical work by hand. Calculator-free arithmetic is part of the exam

sections.title: Chemistry: the most controllable of the three
sections.body:
Chemistry splits cleanly, and each third wants a different approach.

**Physical** — treat it like Physics. Mole concept, Equilibrium and Thermodynamics are the load-bearing chapters, and every numerical rests on the mole concept being automatic.

**Organic** — the single highest-leverage decision in your preparation is to learn General Organic Chemistry properly before touching reactions. With electronic effects and intermediate stability in place, Organic becomes reasoning. Without them it's several hundred reactions to memorise, which is exactly why students find it impossible.

**Inorganic** — largely recall, and the place where NCERT wording matters almost as much as in Biology. Derive from periodic trends where you can; make tables where you can't. It's also the section that decays fastest without revision, so schedule it late and repeatedly.

sections.title: What order to actually study in
sections.body:
The roadmap encodes this, but the principle is worth stating: **follow the dependencies, not the chapter numbers.**

Cell Structure before any Human Physiology. Cell Division before Genetics. Chemical Bonding before anything in Inorganic or Organic. General Organic Chemistry before reactions. Mechanics before everything in Physics.

Anything with no unfinished prerequisites is something you can start today — that's what the map shows you, and it's why a locked topic is locked rather than simply further down a list.

Two chapters worth starting earlier than most people do, because they're long and they compound: **Molecular Basis of Inheritance** and **Carbonyl Compounds**.

sections.title: Revision, and why re-reading fails
sections.body:
Re-reading is the most popular revision method and close to the least effective. It feels productive because the material is familiar, and familiarity is not recall.

What works better:
- **Test yourself first, read second.** Try to state what's in a chapter before opening it. The gaps you find are the revision
- **Space it.** A chapter revisited on day 1, day 7 and day 30 sticks far better than three passes in one week
- **Keep an error notebook.** Every mock mistake, with why you made it — a concept gap, a misread, an arithmetic slip. Rereading this beats rereading anything else, and reviewing it is the habit that most reliably moves a plateaued score
- **Full-length mocks, timed.** 180 questions in 180 minutes is a stamina and pacing skill, separate from knowing the content, and it has to be trained deliberately

sections.title: Advice you'll hear that is wrong
sections.body:
**"Skip Physics, Biology will carry you."** Biology is half the paper, and at the cutoffs that matter almost everyone has good Biology. Physics is what separates ranks.

**"Do every book you can find."** Depth in NCERT plus one good problem source beats breadth across five. Multiple books mostly buy you the illusion of coverage.

**"Study 16 hours a day."** Sustained focused hours beat heroic ones. Someone doing six real hours daily for two years will beat someone doing fourteen for two months and burning out.

**"Solve previous years' papers at the end."** Start them far earlier than feels right. They teach you what the examiner actually values, and every week you delay is a week spent studying without that information.

guides.title: How to actually prepare for JEE
guides.subtitle: Two exams, one syllabus, and the dependency almost everyone discovers too late.
guides.caveat: The JEE syllabus has been revised, with topics both added and removed, and Main and Advanced can differ in scope. Check the official NTA syllabus for Main and the JAB syllabus for Advanced for your exam year before deciding what to skip.

sections.title: Main and Advanced want different things
sections.body:
The syllabus is essentially shared. The papers are not.

**Main** rewards speed, coverage and accuracy on single-concept questions. You are rarely asked something deep; you are asked ninety things quickly. Marks come from not making mistakes.

**Advanced** rewards depth. A single question may need rotational dynamics, energy conservation and integration together, and the answer format punishes partial understanding. Marks come from being able to hold three ideas at once.

The practical consequence: prepare the syllabus for Advanced, then train speed separately for Main. Doing it the other way round — coverage first, depth later — leaves you fast at problems Advanced doesn't ask.

sections.title: Physics failures are usually Maths failures
sections.body:
This is the most useful thing in this guide.

Students hit a wall in Rotational Dynamics, or in Electrostatics, or in AC circuits, and conclude they're bad at Physics. Nearly always the actual gap is upstream:

- **Rotational dynamics** needs integration. Moment of inertia *is* an integral
- **Electrostatics** needs vectors and integration, and its mathematics is identical to gravitation — if one worked and the other didn't, the difference is confidence, not content
- **AC circuits** are SHM in different symbols, and phasors are complex numbers
- **Variable-force problems** in Work-Energy are calculus questions wearing a physics costume

The roadmap makes those prerequisites explicit across subject lines, which a per-subject chapter list structurally cannot. If a Physics chapter feels impossible, check what it needs before grinding at it.

The corollary: **do not defer Calculus.** Limits, Continuity and Integrals early makes half the Physics syllabus easier. Leaving them for Class 12 makes Class 11 Physics harder than it ever needed to be.

sections.title: Maths: half of it is Calculus
sections.body:
Integrals alone are the largest single block of marks in the subject, and Applications of Derivatives is the most directly transferable chapter you'll study.

What matters:
- **Fluency, not familiarity.** Integration is a skill built by volume. There is no way to read your way to it
- **3D Geometry and Vectors are nearly free marks** — formulaic, self-contained, and consistently examined. Front-load them
- **Conic Sections is pattern-heavy.** Once you've seen the standard question types, they repeat
- **Domain discipline.** A large share of "wrong answer, right method" comes from ignoring where a function is defined

sections.title: Chemistry: the most predictable marks in the paper
sections.body:
Chemistry is where a well-prepared student loses the fewest marks, and it splits three ways.

**Physical** — numerical and reliable. Mole concept must be automatic; Equilibrium and Thermodynamics are the load-bearing chapters. Solid State is almost pure arithmetic and among the best value in the syllabus.

**Organic** — learn General Organic Chemistry and stereochemistry *before* reactions. With electronic effects and intermediate stability in place, Organic is deduction; without them it's memorising hundreds of arrows. This single ordering decision determines whether students find Organic tractable or hopeless.

**Inorganic** — recall-heavy and the fastest to decay. Derive from periodic trends where possible. Schedule it late, revisit it often, and don't neglect qualitative analysis: salt analysis and functional group tests are asked directly and are easy marks for anyone who bothered.

sections.title: How to practise
sections.body:
Reading solutions is the most common way to waste study time. It produces recognition, which feels like understanding right up until the exam.

- **Sit with a problem longer than is comfortable.** The struggle is the learning; the solution is just confirmation
- **Previous years' papers, early.** They teach the examiner's habits, which no textbook contains. Every month you delay is a month of studying without knowing what's valued
- **Timed sectional tests** for Main, **untimed multi-chapter problems** for Advanced. Different skills, trained differently
- **An error notebook.** Every mistake with its cause: concept gap, misread question, algebra slip. Reviewing this is the single habit that most reliably lifts a stuck score
- **Write your own formula sheet.** The writing is the revision. A downloaded one is somebody else's memory

sections.title: Advice you'll hear that is wrong
sections.body:
**"Do Physics first, it's the toughest."** Physics is hardest *because of the Maths under it*. Doing it first without calculus is why it feels impossible.

**"Coaching material is enough, skip NCERT."** True for Physics and Maths, false for Inorganic Chemistry, where NCERT wording shows up directly.

**"More questions is always better."** Two hundred problems you fought through and reviewed beat two thousand you skimmed. Volume without review is a hobby.

**"Advanced is just harder Main."** It's a different exam. Multi-concept problems and answer formats that punish partial credit are the difference, and they need practising as their own thing.

**"Drop a subject and focus."** There are no optional subjects. A weak subject caps your rank no matter how strong the other two are.
